name: Malchijah
overview: Malchijah is a male biblical figure uniquely identified as the father of Pashhur and the son of King Zedekiah, as recorded in Jeremiah 38. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His significance arises primarily from his familial connections within the context of Judah's royal lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Malchijah means 'YHWH is [my] king,' reflecting a theocentric identity common in Hebrew names. This proper name is noted in Jeremiah 38:6 and underscores a recognition of God's sovereignty, though it was not explicitly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Malchijah is explicitly identified as the father of Pashhur and the son of King Zedekiah, establishing his position within the royal family. Additionally, he is noted as the father of Mattaniah, further extending his familial line. Beyond these relationships, Scripture does not provide additional family details.
scriptureSignificance: Malchijah's importance in Scripture is tied to his role within the royal family during a critical period in Judah's history. Being both the son of King Zedekiah and the father of Pashhur situates him in the midst of the political and spiritual turmoil recorded in Jeremiah. His name's meaning also reflects the underlying biblical theme of God's kingship during times of national crisis.
